title: The dose that took 21 years — research gap reel
caption:
Ambien sold 21 years before the FDA halved women's bedtime dose (2013). We clear it slower.
Ask if yours is sex-specific.
Send this to your foggiest friend. Groggy mornings — you too?
www.aiforheratx.org
#womenshealth #perimenopause #insomnia #medicationsafety #researchgap

scenes.text: I took the *normal* dose. Nine hours later I'm still driving like I'm half asleep.

scenes.text: Everyone told her it was stress. Nobody asked whether the dose was built for her body.
phrases: Same pill, same box, same dose.

scenes.text: Until 1993, FDA policy kept women of childbearing age out of most early drug trials.
phrases: So morning levels stayed high enough to impair driving.
She wasn't fragile. The data was.

scenes.text: Write down the drug and the dose, then ask your prescriber one question at the refill.
phrases: 1. Ask: "Is this dose different for women?" (FDA, 2013)
2. Ask about CBT-I — first-line for chronic insomnia.
3. A 20-minute daylight walk counts toward WHO's 150 min/week.
